    Styles

    A style is a named set of rules, and a rule says what a marker looks like and which markers it applies to. Groups and markers point at a style rather than carrying a look of their own, so editing one changes everything wearing it.

    Fits none ticked = any group

    Showing on the body

    The top of three levels — this, then each group, then each marker. The first one that does not say as below decides, and nothing beneath it is consulted. Hiding is a body-map idea: the ladder, History, Reports and every export go on reporting every record whatever this says.

    Show on each marker

    Start afresh

    One press returns the under-marker lines to a fresh install. Numbering belongs to each group now — its type and its ordering decide it — and styles and their rules are edited on their own page. Nothing in the log is touched.

    Privacy

    The passcode is a screen, not encryption — the log itself stays readable in this browser’s storage and in any backup file. A forgotten code can request an unlock that opens after 15 minutes, which also means anyone with that long alone with this device could do the same. The cover hides the app from a glance when you switch away; what the system shows in its own task switcher is up to the system.

    Your data

    Your markers are saved in this browser, on this device only — they do not travel with the app when you copy it elsewhere. A backup is one .json file holding every marker, every record made at one, your groups and your settings: back up before you move Jabbity to another device, then restore it there.

    Your log is always saved, whatever this says — it only governs what Jabbity keeps for itself: the undo history that survives a reload, and the safety copies. Once the log is bigger than this, those stop being kept and the app says so.

    Automatic backup

    When this is on, Jabbity saves a copy after every change to a marker and whenever you switch views. It keeps a safety copy of its own on this device, and can also write to a file you choose.

    Dated copies appear here once the first automatic save has run — one per day, the last few kept.

    Two limits worth knowing. The safety copy lives on this device, so it protects you from mistakes inside the app — not from losing the device or clearing your browsing data; keep using Back up to a file for that. And no browser lets a page open your file manager or highlight a file, so Jabbity cannot do that: to find a backup on disk, use Back up to a file and then your browser's own download list, which offers Show in folder.

    About

    Jabbity records a timestamped marker for every tap on the body map. The newest marker is rung 1; older markers move down the ladder. Everything is stored on this device only. Press a marker to log to it; long-press or right-click opens its menu, where the full details live.
